sections.h2: Where is Prince William County, VA, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Prince William County sits on the Potomac River in Northern Virginia and covers 348 square miles, of which 336 are land. Loudoun and Fairfax Counties border it on the north, Fauquier on the west and Stafford on the south, with Charles County, Maryland, across the river (Wikipedia).

The county seat is Manassas, an independent city that sits inside the county. Manassas Park is a second independent city enclosed by it. A house in either city is billed by the city, not by the county, so check the town on the deed before you look up a tax account.

The county elects seven supervisors by magisterial district (Brentsville, Coles, Potomac, Gainesville, Neabsco, Occoquan and Woodbridge) plus an at-large chair. Incorporated towns are Dumfries, Haymarket, Occoquan and Quantico. Dale City is the largest community, and Woodbridge, Lake Ridge, Gainesville and Linton Hall are census-designated places. The western half is a green belt called the rural crescent, which matters if your parcel is larger than a subdivision lot.

sections.h2: Which Prince William County offices handle real estate tax?
sections.html:
Two county offices split the work: the Real Estate Assessments Office sets the value and Taxpayer Services handles bills and payments, both under Tax Administration.

OfficeWhat it doesContact on the county page
Real Estate Assessments OfficeValues property, answers assessment questions, takes correction requests703-792-6780, realestate@pwcgov.org, 4379 Ridgewood Center Drive, Suite 203, Prince William, VA 22192
Taxpayer ServicesBilling and payment questions703-792-6710, TaxpayerServices@pwcgov.org
Board of EqualizationHears real estate assessment appeals after the office reviewAppeal form posted on the county site

The county lists in-person assessment office hours as Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and phone hours as 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Payments are made through the county's Taxpayer Portal. The county also warns against mailing checks because of check washing fraud and suggests paying online (Prince William County real estate tax page).

sections.h2: When is Prince William County real estate tax due?
sections.html:
Prince William County bills real estate tax in two installments a year, and county notices show the first half due July 15 and the second half due December 5.

  • First half of 2026: due July 15, 2026, according to the county's June 22 notice.
  • Second half of 2025: due December 5, 2025.
  • Second half of 2024 and 2022: also due December 5 in the county's notices for those years.

The county's notice page did not show a December 2026 notice when we looked, so confirm the second-half date for this year with Taxpayer Services before you plan a closing around it. Most owners with a mortgage pay through escrow. The county says it bills mortgage servicing companies directly, and if you get a paper bill that your servicer should have received, you are asked to forward it to the servicer (county tax news).

The county also charges a supplemental real estate tax on new improvements finished after the start of the year. A seller who built an addition or finished a basement recently should ask whether a supplemental bill is still coming.

sections.h2: How does Prince William County calculate the real estate tax bill?
sections.html:
The bill is the assessed value divided by 100 and multiplied by the total rate, which the county states per $100 of value.

The Board of County Supervisors sets a county-wide base rate each year, a Fire and Rescue levy, a Mosquito and Forest Pest Management levy, and special district levies that pay for things such as road improvements. Storm water management and solid waste fees are set separately. The county's own worked example uses a rate of $0.9805 per $100 and an assessed value of $607,800, which gives $5,959.48. That figure is an illustration from the county page, not this year's rate, so use the rate on your own bill.

  • Check which special district levies apply to your address.
  • Add storm water and solid waste fees if they appear on the bill.
  • Ask about any supplemental bill for new construction.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Prince William County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the Real Estate Assessments Office, then go to the Board of Equalization, and use the circuit court if you still disagree.

The county's Taxpayer Bill of Rights says owners can examine the working papers behind a value, meet with assessment staff, and request a correction if they think the value is wrong or unfair. It also lists appeals to the Board of Equalization for real estate and to the circuit court (county rights page). Read the notice you received and ask the office.

Virginia law sets the ground rules. The board starts from a presumption that the assessor's value is correct, and the owner must show by a preponderance of the evidence that the property is valued above fair market value or that the assessment is not uniform (Va. Code 58.1-3379). Sales and income evidence up to December 31 before the assessment date can be considered. Separately, a taxpayer can ask the assessing official to correct an erroneous assessment within three years of the end of the tax year or one year from the assessment, whichever is later, but that route covers errors by the assessor, not disagreements over opinion of value (Va. Code 58.1-3980).

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Prince William County property tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate tax follows the house, because Virginia gives the tax a lien ahead of every other lien until it is paid.

State law says the purchaser at a sale, or the trustee in a foreclosure sale, must cause the sale proceeds to be applied to all taxes assessed on the real estate, and that taxes include penalties and interest. The seller's share of the year is prorated by contract, and the treasurer or other proper officer releases the lien (Va. Code 58.1-3340). In practice, the closing agent pays what is owed from the seller's proceeds. Ask Taxpayer Services for a payoff figure that includes the current half before the closing date is set.

The deed also carries a state grantor's tax of 50 cents for each $500 of consideration, paid by the seller unless the contract shifts it to the buyer, and the clerk will not record the deed until it is paid (Va. Code 58.1-802). Prince William County, Manassas and Manassas Park share one Circuit Court clerk, so recording questions for all three go to the same office.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Prince William County usually face?
sections.html:
Most sellers here own their homes and deal with a commuter market tied to Washington, D.C., military employers and a fast-growing tax base.

At the 2020 census the county had 158,525 housing units, 3.0 percent of them vacant, and 71.6 percent of occupied units were owner-occupied. Top employers in the county's 2025 annual financial report include Prince William County Public Schools, the county government, the Department of Defense, Walmart and Sentara Healthcare. The county is also home to Marine Corps Base Quantico and a large concentration of data centers shared with Loudoun County.

  • Commuting: Interstate 66 and Interstate 95 cross the county, along with U.S. 1, U.S. 15, U.S. 29 and State Route 234.
  • Transit: Virginia Railway Express runs a Manassas line and a Fredericksburg line, and PRTC provides OmniRide bus service.
  • Schools: Prince William County Public Schools is the second largest school system in Virginia, and Quantico is served by the Department of Defense Education Activity.

Sellers behind on payments, with inherited property, or with a house that needs work often prefer a direct cash sale because it avoids repair requests from retail buyers. A cash buyer still has to clear the tax lien at closing, so the same payoff steps apply.

faqs.q: When is the first half of Prince William County real estate tax due in 2026?
faqs.a: July 15, 2026, according to the county's June 22, 2026 notice. The second half has been due December 5 in the notices we reviewed for 2022, 2024 and 2025, so confirm the 2026 date with Taxpayer Services.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Prince William County assessment?
faqs.a: The Real Estate Assessments Office at 703-792-6780 or realestate@pwcgov.org. For billing and payment questions, call Taxpayer Services at 703-792-6710.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Prince William County house if I owe property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, because Virginia gives it priority over other liens. Get a payoff amount from Taxpayer Services so the closing agent can include penalties and interest.

faqs.q: Does Prince William County bill houses in Manassas?
faqs.a: No. Manassas and Manassas Park are independent cities surrounded by the county and bill their own real estate tax. Confirm the jurisdiction on your deed or bill.

faqs.q: What can I do if I think my Prince William County value is too high?
faqs.a: Ask the Real Estate Assessments Office to review it, then appeal to the Board of Equalization or the circuit court if needed. Under state law the owner must rebut a presumption that the assessor's value is correct, so bring sales or appraisal evidence.
